title: Recall all multiplication and division facts to 100 quickly

lesson.title: Fast Facts: The Times Table Speed Trick

steps.say: You already know your twos, fives and tens like the back of your hand. Today we make the trickier ones just as fast, using little shortcuts instead of trying to memorize a giant list.

Here is the big secret. Every hard fact is just an easy fact plus one more group. Look at the sixes on the hundred chart. Six times seven looks scary, but five times seven is thirty five, and then you just add one more seven to get forty two.

Let us try a really tough one. Eight times seven. Start with what you know, four times seven is twenty eight. Eight is double four, so just double twenty eight. Twenty eight plus twenty eight is fifty six. So eight times seven is fifty six.

Now the best part. Every division fact is a multiplication fact wearing a costume. If someone asks fifty six divided by eight, do not start counting. Just whisper to yourself, eight times what makes fifty six? Seven! That is your answer, and it takes about one second.

Here is a mistake I see all the time. A friend says nine times six is fifty six. Watch out, that is the eight times seven answer sneaking in! Check it with the nines trick. Ten times six is sixty, then take away one six, and sixty take away six is fifty four. So nine times six is fifty four, not fifty six.

visual.caption: The nines: notice 54 is here, but 56 is not

steps.say: So when a fact feels slow, do not freeze. Lean on a fact you already own, then add one group, double it, or take one group away.

lesson.answer: Every hard fact hides an easy one: add a group, double it, or take a group away — and division is just multiplication asked backwards.

practice.question: At the Richmond farmers market, blueberries cost seven dollars a basket. Ms. Yuanyuan buys eight baskets. First, use doubling to find the total cost: four baskets cost how much, and then double it? Then answer the backwards question: if she spent forty two dollars on baskets at seven dollars each, how many baskets did she buy?
practice.answer: Four baskets cost twenty eight dollars, and doubling gives fifty six dollars for eight baskets. For the second part, seven times six equals forty two, so forty two divided by seven is six baskets.
